the key of this note is printed as an italic b (no descender); no marker b exists in the body, and the body marker q has no note. The b is almost certainly the q sort set upside down; key recorded as printed, b, for marker {q}.

a column of small marks runs down the outer edge of the margin beside the notes keyed o, p and b (after 'c. vij.', 'vxores', 'diuor', 'ſed e', 'nup'), all at one x and all below the baselines of their lines; taken as show-through or set-off, so no final period is transcribed on 'vxores', 'diuor', 'ſed e', 'nup' (reader B read periods after 'diuor', 'nup', 'Iuſtin').

a small ring is printed immediately after 'Iuſtin' at x-height, touching the n: a superscript o abbreviating 'Iuſtinien' (the parallel note keyed r spells 'Iuſti-/nien' out), or a stray mark. Not a baseline period; not transcribed. 'nouuel'/'les' breaks without a hyphen here.
the last letter is heavily inked; read as c ('vt lic.' for vt liceat), could be read as e.
the note with key t has no {t} marker in the body: the marker that should answer it, on 'eſtre par tout repandu de ſa mort', is printed with the u sort (see that entry).
the line is justified and 've' is set as 'v e' with a word-sized gap; closed up as the first syllable of 'velit', continued 'lit.' on the next line.

the note with key x has no {x} marker anywhere in the body (the body carries o p q r ſ u u y). The mark after the opening c is a raised tick, transcribed as an apostrophe (reader B read a period); the citation is c. Veniens, X. de teſtibus.
a smudge of ink sits above 'de'; the word ends in a clear m and period, no tilde (reader B read 'Siquidẽ.').
the foot carries the signature 'A iiij' and no catchword; no foot citation block.
